name: Ashenvale
summary: Ashenvale's sacred woods are now a battleground as the Horde cuts timber for Orgrimmar. The ancient forest lies between the Barrens to the south and Darkshore to the north, under the care of the Sentinels and Cenarius. Its canopy shelters moonwells and old ruins, alongside demonic blights, hostile tribes, and a contested frontier.

sections.title: The Whispering Canopy
sections.body: Beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has belonged to the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius for millennia. Immense trees form a close canopy, turning the daily rain to mist and leaving the forest floor in twilight. Moss covers the ruins of elven settlements, where walking ancients and dryads keep watch. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here. They hunted lightly and kept the wild domain in balance.

sections.title: War for the Woods
sections.body: The Third War broke Ashenvale's peace when Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan entered for lumber. Their demonic bloodlust led them to slay Cenarius. The struggle is now a full territorial war. From Splintertree Post and the southern Mor'shan Rampart, the Warsong Outriders send axes and shredders into the eastern woods to supply Orgrimmar. The Silverwing Sentinels hold Astranaar, a sanctuary town, and have sworn to drive every orcish logger from the sacred grove.

sections.title: Lingering Shadows
sections.body: The lumber war is only one danger in Ashenvale. The Burning Legion left blighted scars at Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Canyon, where Mannoroth died. Satyrs use ruins such as Satyrnaar and Xavian as bases, corrupting waterways and wildlife. Furbolg tribes, once friends of the elves, have largely fallen to dark madness. Mysterious worgen stalk the northern shrine near Felwood, while cursed dragonkin prowl Bough Shadow and guard a portal into the troubled Emerald Dream.

faq.q: Why are the Horde and Alliance fighting in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The Horde needs Ashenvale's timber to build Orgrimmar and sustain its young nation. The orcs of Durotar have little timber in their dry homeland, while the night elves hold Ashenvale as a sacred ancestral home under nature deities' protection. The Silverwing Sentinels see the Warsong clan's clear-cutting as desecration, and the dispute brings skirmishes and pitched fighting in Warsong Gulch.

faq.q: What happened to Cenarius in this forest?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Grommash Hellscream led the Warsong clan into Ashenvale for timber. Cenarius attacked to defend the sacred grove. Desperate to defeat the demigod, Grommash and his clan drank from a fountain tainted by the pit lord Mannoroth. The demonic fury they gained let them slay Cenarius. Grom later broke the curse by killing Mannoroth at Demon Fall Canyon, but the elves have not forgotten their patron demigod's murder.

Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath the Zoram Strand on Ashenvale's northwestern coast. The sunken temple was once an ancient kaldorei temple to Elune, then collapsed into the sea during the Great Sundering. Savage naga, Twilight's Hammer cultists, and aquatic beasts now overrun it and revere the ancient hydra Aku'mai.

faq.q: What is the Great Tree at Bough Shadow?
faq.answer: Bough Shadow holds one of four Great Trees planted by the Cenarion Circle thousands of years ago to anchor conduits into the Emerald Dream. The tree remains an active gateway between Azeroth and the Dream. Green dragonspawn guard the area, though a sinister taint in the Dream sometimes sends monstrous Nightmare Dragons through the portal.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Ashenvale hostile?
faq.answer: The furbolgs of Ashenvale were peaceful allies of the night elves for centuries, until demonic taint from the Burning Legion's invasion shattered their minds. Fel magic lingering from places such as Felwood, Satyrnaar, and Demon Fall Canyon drove tribes like the Thistlefur into violent madness. They turned against outsiders and their own kin.

faq.q: Who is buried at Demon Fall Canyon?
faq.answer: Demon Fall Canyon is where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall faced the pit lord Mannoroth. Grom struck the demon lord a fatal blow, freeing the orcish race from the demonic blood curse at the cost of his life. A monument to Grom Hellscream stands there, and many orcs make pilgrimage to honor the warrior who freed their people.

faq.q: How do I travel through Ashenvale?
faq.answer: Alliance travelers usually enter Ashenvale through the northern mountain pass from Auberdine in Darkshore, then follow the highway east toward Astranaar. Horde travelers march north from the Barrens through the fortified Mor'shan Rampart toward Splintertree Post, or west to Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand. Both factions keep flight masters at their major fortresses.

angles.text: As a night elf, Ashenvale is your spiritual homeland and the legacy of Cenarius. Defending its groves from Warsong axes and clearing satyr corruption from its moonwells are matters of kaldorei honor.
As an orc, this timber supplies the walls and siege towers of Orgrimmar. Ashenvale is also sacred ground where Grommash Hellscream shed blood to free the orcish race from demonic servitude.

As a druid, you see nature's balance under attack from many sides. Lumber operations, corrupted furbolg dens, and the nightmare-haunted portal at Bough Shadow all leave Ashenvale in need of Cenarion restoration.

As a herbalist, you find rich gathering grounds in Ashenvale, fed by ancient magical leyways and steady rain. Briarthorn, Stranglekelp, and Kingsblood grow here, with rare Gromsblood near demonic scars.
